key_insight: QAOA on MaxCut shows entanglement scaling that matches fermionic Gaussian-state behavior when properly optimized, while adiabatic optimization exhibits distinctly schedule-dependent entanglement patterns.
engineering_relevance: Better optimizer choice can materially change observed quantum resources, so algorithm benchmarking and hardware-oriented tuning must account for entanglement scaling as a performance diagnostic.
method: Studied QAOA on MaxCut across a broad set of problem instances.
Compared entanglement profiles under different variational training quality, using a high-performance optimizer.
Benchmarked QAOA against adiabatic quantum computation with varying annealing schedules.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports empirical evidence that well-trained QAOA entanglement scaling follows fermionic Gaussian-state scaling up to a factor, while poor training can obscure that trend.
watch_item: Observed entanglement behavior is sensitive to optimizer quality and annealing schedule, so conclusions may shift with different training or control protocols.
paper_title: Entanglement Scaling and Problem Structure in Quantum Approximate and Adiabatic Optimization Algorithms
